method: A statute that names coercive control does not finish the work.
The hard part is showing the pattern in a longitudinal record.
Conflict, including hostility, is not that pattern.
Carlton Research, LLC does not represent parties and does not make parenting-time recommendations.
usaTodayErrors: The USA Today roundup dated April 24, 2026 listed Kentucky, Louisiana, and Maine as having or pushing laws. Those three do not have a named-term statute. The roundup missed Washington (2022 civil). The roundup could not list the Arizona, Utah, or New Hampshire 2026 enactments, which post-date the story. Oklahoma custody 2024 was also missing.

instruments.accomplishes: Hawaii creates a standalone petty misdemeanor for coercive control under HRS 709-906(6), in force through June 30, 2031.
instruments.notes: Act 238 of 2021 created the offence. Act 192 of 2026 continues the statute through June 30, 2031. Hawaii is the only U.S. jurisdiction with a named-term criminal offence in force on this tracker.

instruments.accomplishes: Hawaii writes coercive control into HRS 586-1, so a civil protective order may rest on the named term (Act 20, 2020).
California writes coercive control into Family Code 6320 (SB 1141, 2020; SB 374, 2021; SB 50, 2025), so a domestic violence restraining order may rest on the named term.
Connecticut writes coercive control into C.G.S. 46b-1 and 46b-15 through Jennifer's Law, PA 21-78, signed June 28, 2021, so a civil restraining order may rest on the named term.
Connecticut custody determinations under C.G.S. 46b-56 draw on the coercive control definition written into 46b-1 by Jennifer's Law, PA 21-78, signed June 28, 2021.
Washington writes coercive control into RCW 7.105.010 (SHB 1901, effective July 1, 2022), so a domestic violence protection order may rest on the named term.
Vermont writes coercive controlling behavior into 15 V.S.A. 1101 (Act 103, effective July 1, 2024), so a relief-from-abuse order may rest on the named term.
instruments.notes: The statutory phrase is coercive controlling behavior, which meets the named-term rule.

instruments.accomplishes: Vermont parenting determinations under 15 V.S.A. 665a draw on the coercive controlling behavior definition in 15 V.S.A. 1101 (Act 103, July 1, 2024).
Massachusetts writes coercive control into G.L. c. 209A section 1 (Acts 2024 c. 118, effective September 18, 2024), so an abuse-prevention order may rest on the named term.

New Jersey directs a court considering a final restraining order to consider a pattern of coercive control under N.J.S.A. 2C:25-29(a)(7) (P.L. 2023 c. 230, January 8, 2024). The pattern is not a standalone predicate act.
New Hampshire writes coercive control into RSA 173-B:1 (HB 1522, Chapter 230, signed July 2, 2026). A court may consider the pattern. The petitioner still needs a credible present threat.
Oklahoma requires custody and visitation determinations to consider coercive control under 43 O.S. 109 (SB 901, effective November 1, 2024).
Colorado writes coercive control article-wide at C.R.S. 14-10-103 (HB26-1309, Chapter 163, signed May 27, 2026). The session law date is May 27, 2026, not August 12, 2026.
Utah requires custody determinations to consider coercive control under Utah Code 81-9-101 and 81-9-204/206 (HB 303, signed March 23, 2026).
Arizona requires custody determinations to consider coercive control under A.R.S. 25-403.03 (HB 2995, signed June 22, 2026, emergency).
New York S4079 / A679 (2025-26) would create a class E felony of coercive control. The bill remains in committee. The session runs through December 31, 2026.
New York S08633-A / A09551-A would add coercive control on a civil track. The companion remains in committee for the 2025-26 session.
South Carolina S.702 (Mica's Law) failed in 2026. The sponsor announced on June 25, 2026 a January 2027 reintroduction of a coercive control bill.
Kentucky 25RS HB 96 died in Rules on February 27, 2025. Death in Rules is not a veto. No named-term coercive control statute is in force.
Louisiana R.S. 46:2132(3) does not say coercive control. Secondary lists that treat Louisiana as a named-term jurisdiction overstate the statute.
Maine LD 670 was enacted as coercion in 19-A MRSA 4102. The enacted text does not use the named term coercive control.
Pennsylvania Act 8 of 2024 (Kayden's Law) does not use the words coercive control. Pennsylvania state Kayden's Law is not federal.
West Virginia HB 5336 died in House Judiciary when the 2026 session adjourned. No named-term coercive control statute is in force.
Maryland HB 1586 (2026) had a hearing and no floor vote. No named-term coercive control statute is in force.
Rhode Island S 2489 (2026) died at adjournment. No named-term coercive control statute is in force.

Illinois HB 4659 kept DOMESTIC VIOL-COERCIVE CONTROL in the title. A Senate amendment stripped coercive control. Final text of PA 104-0556 is coerced-debt under the Consumer Installment Loan Act, effective January 1, 2027.
Florida CS/CS/HB 277, Chapter 2026-86, effective July 1, 2026, does not define coercive control in the enrolled text. The chapter is not scored as a named-term law.

England and Wales create a criminal offence where a person repeatedly or continuously engages in controlling or coercive behaviour toward a personally connected person (Serious Crime Act 2015 s.76, in force 29 December 2015).
instruments.notes: UK statutory phrase: controlling or coercive behaviour.

instruments.accomplishes: Ireland creates a criminal offence of coercive control under Domestic Violence Act 2018 s.39, in force 1 January 2019.

Gibraltar creates a criminal offence of repeatedly or continuously engaging in controlling or coercive behaviour toward a personally connected person (Domestic Abuse Act 2023 s.3, in force 6 July 2023).
instruments.notes: UK statutory phrase: controlling or coercive behaviour.

instruments.accomplishes: New South Wales creates a 7-year offence of a course of abusive behaviour against a current or former intimate partner at Crimes Act 1900 s.54D, in force 1 July 2024.

instruments.instrument: Criminal Law (Coercive Control and Affirmative Consent) and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
instruments.accomplishes: Queensland creates a coercive control offence at Criminal Code s.334C, commenced 26 May 2025, with a maximum of 14 years, covering an intimate partner, family member, or informal carer.

Canada enacts a Criminal Code offence of coercive or controlling conduct toward an intimate partner (Bill C-16, Protecting Victims Act, Royal Assent June 18, 2026). The offence remains not in force for up to two years after Royal Assent.
instruments.notes: Justice labels the item coercive control. Statute text uses coercive or controlling conduct. Not in force as of August 31, 2026.

instruments.accomplishes: Scotland creates a course-of-behaviour domestic abuse offence under the Domestic Abuse (Scotland) Act 2018 s.1. The statute does not use coercive control or controlling or coercive behaviour.

instruments.instrument: Domestic Abuse and Civil Proceedings Act (Northern Ireland) 2021 s.1
instruments.citation: Domestic Abuse and Civil Proceedings Act (Northern Ireland) 2021 s.1
instruments.accomplishes: Northern Ireland creates a domestic abuse offence under the 2021 Act s.1. The statute does not use coercive control or controlling or coercive behaviour.

instruments.citation: Divorce Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 3 (2nd Supp.), s.2(1)
instruments.accomplishes: The Canada Divorce Act defines family violence to include a pattern of coercive and controlling behaviour. That definition is family law, not a criminal named-term offence, and is not scored as named-term in force.

New Zealand includes coercive or controlling behaviour in the Family Violence Act 2018 definition of family violence. That inclusion is civil and definitional. The Act does not create a standalone criminal offence of coercive control.
instruments.notes: Do not count New Zealand in the headline criminal-in-force country total.

instruments.instrument: Criminal Law Consolidation (Coercive Control) Amendment Act 2025
instruments.citation: No 35 of 2025, s.2 commencement by proclamation
instruments.accomplishes: South Australia enacted a standalone coercive control offence through the Criminal Law Consolidation (Coercive Control) Amendment Act 2025 (No 35 of 2025). Commencement awaits a day fixed by proclamation, so the offence is not in force.
instruments.notes: AustLII s.2: the Act comes into operation on a day to be fixed by proclamation.
